campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) to accept low-carbon transportation program funding for a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also touched on pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a low-carbon transportation and operations program fund agreement with VTA for transit reliability and performance improvements
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes, vendor payments, and a conflict of interest code update, along with final map approvals for two residential lot splits. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential development projects, and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming public town halls.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for two-lot subdivisions at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of a Design Review and setback variance approval for a single-family home and ADU at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of a Tentative Map, Design Review, and CEQA exemption for a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of town hall meetings on September 19 and 30
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine business including updated employee pay schedules, a funding increase for an electrical maintenance contractor, and reorganizing the volunteer awards committee. Council also considered renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, discussed a citizen initiative on zoning impacts, and set up a subcommittee to handle the City Manager's annual performance review.
keyTopics: Resolution renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Amendment No. 4 increasing the Bear Electrical Solutions maintenance contract by $250,000
Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee associations and unrepresented staff
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning
Disbanding the Joint Volunteer Awards Committee and creating a Los Altos-only version

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine administrative matters, including approval of previous meeting minutes and the town's July 2026 financial report. The Council also considered several service and professional contracts, including an amendment related to HVAC (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) work and multiple professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Closed Session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026, including a correction
Second amendment to an existing town agreement
First amendment to a Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) services agreement
New professional services agreements for the Town Manager to execute

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 16, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to set the agendas for the September 22 and September 29, 2026 City Council meetings and reviewed the public record for a recent week. The committee also considered approving several city-sponsored special events allowing use of city funds and donations, along with a proposal on self-checkout safety standards at grocery and drug stores.
keyTopics: Setting the final agenda for September 22, 2026 and draft agenda for September 29, 2026 Council meetings
Free use of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for the SCCAOR 2026 Fall General Membership Meeting, sponsored by Council District 9
Retroactive approval of the Santos Family Car Show as a Council District 4 sponsored special event
Retroactive approval of various Council District 5 sponsored special events
Proposed self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee met to take public comments, do a team-building exercise, and review its proposed work plan for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Committee members and staff also shared updates and discussed upcoming meetings of other city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Public oral communications on non-agenda items
Team Builder exercise for committee members
Fiscal Year 2026-27 Youth Advisory Committee Work Plan
Committee and staff comments and reports
Review of agendas from other city boards, commissions, and committees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a special morning session of the Sunnyvale City Council focused on the annual 'State of the City' event. The agenda was brief, covering the event schedule before the special meeting was adjourned.
keyTopics: State of the City special meeting and event schedule

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss a closed-session real estate negotiation with the Cupertino Union School District over property at 10480 Finch Avenue, along with anticipated litigation. The public portion covered a range of routine business, including a new AI use policy for the Council, appointments to a subcommittee for selecting a city lobbyist, and a response to a county grand jury report on pothole damage claims.
keyTopics: Closed-session negotiation with Cupertino Union School District over price and terms for property at 10480 Finch Avenue
Closed-session discussion of anticipated litigation
Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy
Appointment of Mayor Moore and Councilmember Wang to a subcommittee to evaluate city lobbyist proposals for 2027-2028
Approval of the city's response to a Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims processes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: Santa Clara's City Council held a special meeting that began with interviews to fill two seats on the Civil Service Commission, followed by a joint meeting with the Stadium Authority Board. The joint session included recognition of outgoing board and commission members and campaign sponsors, along with several routine business items including a janitorial services contract, a historic preservation agreement, and annual commission workplans.
keyTopics: Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission (one partial term through 2028, one full term through 2030)

Recognition of outgoing commissioners from the Library Trustees, Civil Service Commission, Cultural Commission, Historical and Landmarks Commission, Parks and Recreation Commission, and Senior Advisory Commission
Recognition of 2026 Mission Meets the Moment Campaign sponsors
Authorization for the City Manager to negotiate and execute amendments to the citywide janitorial services agreement with Impec Group, Inc.
A Mills Act historic preservation agreement for the property at 1261 Jackson Street

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered several financial and infrastructure items, including the city's use of federal Community Development Block Grant funding, the condition of the Milpitas Community Center, and financing actions related to the former Redevelopment Agency. The Council also received a presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Resolution authorizing the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission — September 9, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission considered a proposed ordinance amending city code to address City Council direction on the separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The Commission also received a Director's Report covering upcoming meeting schedules and commissioner assignments, and reviewed draft minutes from its August 12, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Proposed ordinance amending Municipal Code Titles 18 and 21 regarding separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs)
Director's Report on meeting schedule and commissioner assignments
Approval of draft summary minutes from the August 12, 2026 meeting
